seo_title: DGFT Bans Lithium Battery Black Mass Exports From India
title: DGFT Bars Export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass to Keep Critical Minerals at Home
case_name: Amendment to the export policy for lithium-ion battery black mass under ITC (HS) Code 85491400
card_summary: DGFT changed the export policy for lithium-ion battery black mass under ITC (HS) code 85491400 from 'Free' to 'Prohibited', effective 10 November 2026. The notification covers battery scrap free of lead, cadmium and mercury that still holds recoverable critical minerals. The stated aim is to keep this material in India for domestic recycling and mineral recovery.
card_tip: Exporters and recyclers holding lithium-ion battery black mass should check the Para 1.05 transitional window before shipping; contracts assuming the earlier 'Free' export status now need review against this prohibition.
verification_notes: AUDIENCE: domestic (relevant also to foreign battery and recycling companies sourcing black mass from India). TARGET QUERY: can lithium-ion battery scrap be exported from India / DGFT ban on battery black mass exports. DEMAND EVIDENCE: none seen (no search-volume or trending signal observed; picked for freshness and as a distinct Power, Energy & Mining item). Facts (the change from 'Free' to 'Prohibited', the HS code, the exclusion of lead/cadmium/mercury-bearing scrap, the immediate effect from 10 November 2026, and the stated critical-mineral-recovery rationale) are consistent across a2ztaxcorp, Deccan Herald and several other independent outlets (Maritime Gateway, Energetica India, Inc42, YourStory) that all report the same Notification No. 49/2026-27; World Trade Scanner hosts what it presents as the notification text itself. The notification text was not independently opened on the DGFT's own website. No exemption or phase-in beyond the standard Para 1.05 transitional arrangement was reported.
